{"code": "from collections import Counter

# Re-evaluate premises
print("Verifying premises:")
print(f"'new' segment exists: {'new' in df['customer_segment'].unique()}")
print(f"'paid_search' channel exists: {'paid_search' in df['channel'].unique()}")
print(f"'converted' is 1 only for completed checkout: {set(df.loc[df['converted'] == 1, 'status'].unique()) == {'completed'}}")
print(f"'refunded' orders are not counted as conversions: {set(df.loc[df['converted'] == 1, 'status'].unique()) == {'completed'}}")

# Re-check the definition of 'converted'
# If 'converted' is 1 only when status is 'completed', then for 'refunded' orders, 'converted' must be 0
# So we can use 'converted' directly as the indicator

# Correct approach: population = all orders from new + paid_search
population_df = df[(df['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (df['customer_segment'] == 'new')]
n_total = len(population_df)

# Convert is 1 only for completed checkouts, 0 otherwise (including refunded)
n_converted = population_df['converted'].sum()
fraction = n_converted / n_total if n_total > 0 else 0.0

print(f"Total orders (new + paid_search): {n_total}")
print(f"Number of converted orders: {n_converted}")
print(f"Fraction converted: {fraction:.4f}")"}
